# switch, restore, and checkout

After this page you can change branches with `git switch` and files with `git restore`, and you can translate an old `git checkout` line.

## Two commands, two jobs

Until Git 2.23, `git checkout` did both jobs. It still does, including in Git 2.55. Checking out a branch moves `HEAD`. Checking out a path copies bytes. One word for both is how a file gets overwritten when the goal was to change branches.

`git switch` moves `HEAD` and refuses a path. `git restore` copies bytes and leaves `HEAD` where it is.

| Older command | Command in this book |
|---------------|----------------------|
| `git checkout main` | `git switch main` |
| `git checkout -b feat/x` | `git switch -c feat/x` |
| `git checkout -- README.md` | `git restore README.md` |
| `git checkout HEAD -- README.md` | `git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- README.md` |
| `git checkout <hash>` | `git switch --detach <hash>` |

Scripts and old notes still say `checkout`. Translate them with the table. Type `switch` and `restore` yourself.

## Switch branches

```bash
cd ~/desk/desk-api
git switch main
git switch -c feat/switch-lab
git switch main
git switch -
git branch --show-current
```

`git switch -` uses `@{-1}`, the checkout you were on before this one. The last command prints `feat/switch-lab`.

```bash
git switch main
git branch -d feat/switch-lab
```

`-d` deletes a branch whose tip is already reachable from `HEAD`. You are on `main`, and `feat/switch-lab` names that same commit, so the delete succeeds.

## A path is not a branch

```bash
git switch README.md
```

Git stops with `fatal: invalid reference: README.md`. The file is unchanged.

## Local edits that would be overwritten

```bash
git switch -c feat/switch-lab
echo "other side" >> README.md
git add README.md
git commit -m "lab: other side"
git switch main
echo "main side" >> README.md
git switch feat/switch-lab
```

Git aborts. The message still says the files would be overwritten by checkout. `README.md` on `main` still ends with `main side`. `feat/switch-lab` still has `other side`.

```bash
git restore README.md
git branch -D feat/switch-lab
git status
```

`-D` deletes a branch even when `main` does not contain its commits. Use it here to discard the throwaway `lab: other side` commit. When you need to keep the uncommitted line and still change branches, stash it (chapter 12).

## Detached HEAD

```bash
git switch --detach HEAD
git switch main
```

`--detach` points `HEAD` at a commit and at no branch. Chapter 1 is the trap: a commit made there needs a new branch before you leave it. From a detached `HEAD` with no new commit, `git switch main` attaches you again.

The lab next walks one scratch commit through soft, mixed, and hard, then brings it back from the reflog.
